description: Create the real React (Vite) 'Coffee Ship' SPA under container/frontend/ plus a session4-specific architecture.svg under container/, matching the session3 look/feel but reflecting THIS demo's services (CodePipeline, CodeBuild, ECR, ECS/Fargate, ALB, CloudFront, DynamoDB, SQS, AppConfig, SSM, Secrets Manager). No auth, no AWS SDK. This is the pure-frontend unit; it is independent of the container Python changes except that FEAT-002 bakes its dist output. There is NO pre-existing architecture.svg in session4 (only session3 has one, with the wrong services), so this feature CREATES one.

findings:
SPA created at container/frontend/ (React 18.3.1 + react-dom 18.3.1, vite 5.4.0, @vitejs/plugin-react 4.3.1; type=module; NO aws-amplify). Entry src/main.jsx imports './styles.css' and renders <App/>. vite.config.js: base '/', build.outDir 'dist'. index.html title 'Coffee Ship', mounts #root, loads /src/main.jsx (no external config.js). `npm run build` writes dist/index.html + dist/assets/{index-<hash>.js, index-<hash>.css} (hashed filenames). FEAT-002 Dockerfile must COPY frontend/dist -> /app/static and architecture.svg -> /app/static/architecture.svg so the app serves them same-origin.

API CONTRACT the SPA depends on (app.py must preserve): POST '/order' with JSON {orderId:<string>, total:<number>} expects 200 {orderId, points}; GET '/health' expects JSON possibly containing a 'version' field; GET '/architecture.svg' expects the svg with Content-Type image/svg+xml.

APP_VERSION / UI version string: the SPA shows the version in the header tag ('live · <version>'). It reads GET /health's `version` field at runtime; if absent/unreachable it falls back to the baked-in constant VERSION = 'v1' (in src/App.jsx). So when FEAT-002 adds APP_VERSION to app.py's /health response, that value is what the header displays live; the baked-in fallback students see offline is exactly the string 'v1'. For the Act 4 'version bump is visible' demo to show a CHANGE, APP_VERSION should start at 'v1' (matching the fallback) and be bumped from there.

architecture.svg created at container/architecture.svg (hand-authored, well-formed XML, no embedded PNG icons): source.zip(S3) -> CodePipeline -> CodeBuild(docker) -> ECR -> rolling deploy to ECS/Fargate -> ALB -> CloudFront -> Users, with the note 'ALB security group allows the CloudFront prefix list only', plus DynamoDB/SQS/AppConfig/SSM/Secrets Manager. Reflects session4 services (no Cognito/ElastiCache).
